thread:
elaine: Quick sync — I'm landing a docs PR that adds a short 'staged contributor' checklist for dedicated capacity onboarding (provisioning + autoscale examples). Before I merge I need: a) SDK snippet sanity check, b) anchor hygiene & redirects, c) a short SLA phrasing note for legal. TL;DR: small, actionable, and safe to backport.

mike: I can review SDK snippets (python + ts). Which branch/PR?

elaine: PR is open: https://git.internal/r/redwood/docs/pulls/442. Branch: docs/ded-cap-staged-checklist. Focus areas: sample terraform, autoscale yaml snippet, and the python SDK example for reserve calls.

samir: Heads-up — if you change any anchors we need to add redirects in docs/config/redirects.yaml or the handbook will 404 in support threads. I can run the link checker after small edits.

ashley: For SLA wording, legal suggested avoiding "guaranteed" unless backed by Dedicated contract. Proposed: "targeted latency SLOs with SLA options for Dedicated customers". Short and conservative.

elaine: Good call. I'll swap out one line to: "targeted latency SLOs; Dedicated customers can opt for contractual SLAs."

mike: Quick nit on SDK: python snippet uses old param name `capacity_token`. New SDK uses `reservation_token`. Also include a minimal `try/except` for auth errors. Example I propose:```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
try:
    r = client.reserve_capacity(reservation_token='abc123', region='us-west')
    print(r.id)
except AuthenticationError:
    print('auth failed')
```

elaine: perfect, thanks. I'll replace and push.

samir: Also add a tiny note for anchor naming convention: use kebab-case and prefix with the doc short id, e.g., `ded-cap-onboard-autoscale` so future moves are easier to map. I'll drop a short snippet in the PR description.

ashley: One more: there's an internal security note about KMS key rotation example. We shouldn't paste customer-specific commands; keep a link to KMS integration guide and a 1-line reminder: "rotate keys per org policy."

elaine: will do. I'll swap out the detailed command with: "See KMS integration guide (internal link). Rotate keys per org policy." and add a sentence to the staged checklist: "If your private deployment uses customer-managed KMS, add a rotation policy to the onboarding ticket."

docs-bot: link-checker queued for PR 442. Run ID: lc-2026-04-12-77. Results will be posted here.

mike: I ran the snippets locally. Two tiny things: the terraform example uses an outdated provider block and the YAML autoscale example lacked the `cooldown_seconds` field. I can send a tiny patch.

elaine: please do, mike. If you send commits to the same branch I'll fast-merge after link-checker green and samir verifies redirects.

samir: link-checker flagged one anchor collision: `#autoscale-policy` already used in capacity-handbook. I suggest renaming to `#ded-cap-autoscale-policy` and adding a redirect entry: `- from: /docs/capacity#autoscale-policy
  to: /docs/dedicated#ded-cap-autoscale-policy`

elaine: adding that to the PR description. Anything else?

ashley: Could we add a 1-sentence example of isolation decorators for tenant configs? Many readers ask where to set them. Keep it high-level: `isolation: tenant` + link to the runtime isolation page.

elaine: yep I'll add one line: "Use `isolation: tenant` to reserve per-tenant resources; see runtime isolation docs for details."

docs-bot: link-checker result: 3 warnings (anchors), 0 errors. Next steps: samir to approve redirect edits; mike to push small patches; ashley to confirm SLA phrasing.

mike: pushed patch for terraform/provider and added `cooldown_seconds: 60` to autoscale YAML.

samir: pushed redirects.yaml entry and ran full link-check. Now clean.

ashley: approve SLA phrasing.

elaine: merging in 10 if no objections. Thanks everyone — keeping this one tiny so it can land and be backported to the handbook. :shipit:

mike: :thumbsup:

samir: :eyes: good job.

ashley: :100:
